claims.text: HfNbTaTiZr is homogeneous, single-phase, disordered, and BCC in the proposed initial state.
Thermally activated edge-dislocation super-jogs form in HfNbTaTiZr at elevated temperatures.
Local atomic-scale inhomogeneities may enhance super-jog formation.
Super-jogs act as strong barriers to further dislocation motion.
Super-jog formation stabilizes the yield strength of HfNbTaTiZr at elevated temperatures.
Super-jog formation stabilizes the elastic moduli of HfNbTaTiZr at elevated temperatures.
Super-jog formation stabilizes the thermal-expansion behavior of HfNbTaTiZr at elevated temperatures.
The disordered lattice distributes strain more uniformly and thereby modulates thermal expansion.
HfNbTaTiZr should exhibit a yield-strength plateau or near-temperature-independent yield strength between roughly 673 K and 1073 K.
HfNbTaTiZr should exhibit a plateau or near-temperature-independent elastic modulus between roughly 673 K and 1073 K.
HfNbTaTiZr should exhibit anomalous nonlinear thermal expansion at elevated temperatures.
Increasing temperature generally makes dislocation motion easier and causes mechanical strength to decline in conventional BCC materials.
Yield strength in BCC pure metals and dilute BCC alloys is controlled by screw-dislocation motion through thermally activated double-kink nucleation.
Below roughly 673 K, traditional dislocation dynamics dominate the response of HfNbTaTiZr.
Above roughly 1073 K, diffusion-driven or other high-temperature phenomena may interfere with the proposed mechanism.
Direct visualization of thermally activated edge-dislocation super-jogs in HfNbTaTiZr is limited.
The quantitative contribution of super-jogs relative to short-range order and other strengthening mechanisms is not established.
